title: STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSAL FOR GSTP ELEMENT 2: MAKE ACTIVITIES
description: The activities in GSTP Element 2 "Make" aim to strengthen worldwide competitiveness in the near term in existing markets, establish strategic capabilities which will result in stronger competitiveness in the medium term on existing or new markets, and to support the implementation of National priorities. GSTP Element 2 "Make" aims to support design, development, and demonstration activities. Products and technologies are defined to be any hardware, software, or applications within the scope set out in section 3 below. Key characteristics of this Element are:  The role of industry in defining and proposing projects oriented to commercial or institutional opportunities in all areas of satellite applications except satellite telecommunication (not covered by GSTP);  The outcome of an activity will eventually become a product ready for exploitation.  The sharing of funding by ESA and industry. Activities submitted in the frame of GSTP Element 2 Make" may be related to the improvement or development of satellite subsystems or equipment (including EGSE), space transportation subsystems or equipment up to engineering model or qualification model, and the improvement or development of ground / user system and equipment up to prototypes and commercialized products. Activities should address any the following technology themes: Earth observation, science, exploration, human spaceflight, space transportation, satellite navigation or generic technologies.

title: TWELFTH FIXED CALL FOR PROPOSALS UNDER THE PLAN FOR EUROPEAN COOPERATING STATES (PECS) IN BULGARIA
description: The European Space Agency and the Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation of the Republic of Bulgaria hereby invite you to submit a proposal for the above Call for Proposals, which will be soon published in esa-star. While it is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, this CfP will be addressed only to Bulgarian legal entities registered in ESA-STAR, as prime tenderer and foresees the following standard activity types: Type A Research and Preparatory Activities, aimed at the preparation for participation in ESA optional programmes or the initial steps of a product development for Space, with potential for use on future ESA missions or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 1 and the target TRL shall be TRL3 or below. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. Type B Flight- and Ground Segment-related Research and Development Activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 3 and the target TRL shall be TRL 6. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 500,000 (hardware development)/EUR 250,000 (all other activities). Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000.Type E: Phase 0/A/B1 small sat mission definition studies with potential to lead to either a national or a commercial mission, in the area of Earth Observation for Climate, Agriculture, Disaster Management and Environmental Monitoring, enabling the development and demonstration of Bulgarian technologies and products in space. Maximum price for ESA 300.000 Euros. Type F Space Applications, products and services making use of ESA/ European space infrastructure that is already existing or scheduled for operation in the near term. The start TRL shall be at least 6 and the target TRL shall be TRL 8. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity. Type G1 University courses/modules leading to a qualification (BSc or MSc) in space related topics that correspond to the needs of national space industry and to encourage career in space and answer to national space industry needs. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 70,000. To be published as a separate tender in esa-star: Type G2 PhD Theses that correspond to a clear need from the national space industry and would lead to a new product or service being able to be developed. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000 with a minimum company co-funding of EUR 10,000. More information and further programmatic constraints can be consulted in the cover letter of the call upon its issue date.

title: GSTP ELEMENT 1: DEVELOP: PREPARATION OF ENABLING SPACE TECHNOLOGIES AND BUILDING BLOCKS - STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSAL
description: The European Space Agency ("the Agency" or "ESA") invites you to submit a Proposal under the General Support Technology Programme, Element 1: "Preparation of enabling space technologies and building blocks''The aim is to prepare and to develop enabling capabilities and the associated building blocks for space related systems and the associated sub-systems. An additional aim is to allow the targeted and coordinated development of the capabilities and building blocks (i.e. among academia and industry) in a given ESA Member State or across different Member States (in a collaborative manner). The intended output is to provide industry with a stronger foundation (i.e. building on this acquired know-how) in order to contribute to new space related system opportunities at national or international levels (institutional, commercial...) The objective is to enable Member States to support the further development of t capabilities and the associated building blocks in their industry. The technology development activities may be prepared in a targeted and coordinated manner. The enabling capabilities and building blocks are to be developed for a targeted type and class of space systems (in terms of performance, cost, size...) and with guiding specifications. The developments are to be performed in a coordinated manner to ensure that industry is able to work on complementary capabilities. title: INCUBED CALL FOR PROPOSAL: STANDARD CALL FOR PROPOSALS
description: The InCubed Element of the European Earth Watch Programme (InCubed) aims to accompany European economic operators in the rapid evolution of the Earth Observation market, both in Europe and globally. InCubed introduces a dedicated process within ESA Earth Observation programmes to strengthen and stimulate the development of near-to-market commercial initiatives in partnership with industry. Activities supported under InCubed include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (e.g. missions, instruments, prototype elements of EO constellations), innovative mission management solutions (including for future EO constellations), as well as the development of ground, data, and application platforms. InCubed targets commercial viability by the end of the activity (at least at minimum viable product level) and requires a substantial degree of innovation, i.e. the creation of new value within the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement is mandatory, with customers acting as beta testers and validators of the developed product or service. Customer engagement must be clearly demonstrated at both pitch and proposal stages, and letters of support or interest from potential customers are considered a strong asset. The scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves, in line with the objectives of InCubed. Two development cycles are available within InCubed, depending on the maturity of the concept: De-risking Cycle (typically starting from TRL 4), focusing on reducing technical and market risks;Product Development Cycle (typically starting from TRL 6), aiming at delivering a product ready for commercialisation. Under this Call for Proposals, economic operators are invited to submit their ideas via the OSIP (Open Space Innovation Platform) (ideas.esa.int), which serves as the entry point for the programme. The application process consists of the following step: Idea Pitch - Applicantssubmit and present a draft Outline proposal via OSIP to ESA (and potentially the relevant National Delegation(s)). Following a positive assessment, economic operators will be invited to submit a Proposal Part 2 (Full) in accordance with the established procedures and evaluation criteria. Activities supported under InCubed are based on a co-funding scheme, whereby economic operators contribute financially to the project, demonstrating commitment to and confidence in their business case.

title: SPACE FOR SUSTAINABLE INDUSTRY AND DIGITAL BUSINESS TRANSFORMATION POC STUDIES - FIXED CALL FOR PROPOSALS
description: The ACCESS Business Applications and Space Solutions (BASS) programme supports the development and commercialisation of innovative services that leverage space assets and technologies to address real-world business challenges.Through this Contest, ESA seeks to accelerate the adoption of space-enabled solutions by connecting companies with leading industry partners [SC1] (i.e. the Challenge-Owners) that have identified specific operational needs and innovation opportunities.The Contest provides a direct pathway for companies to develop and validate Proof of Concept solutions with prospective end users, reducing both technical and commercial risk.
